# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Hope's Retreat for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## The Diversion Nobody meant to settle here. The people who founded Hope's Retreat were passengers on a colonial transport bound somewhere else, until word reached the ship that the place they were going to no longer existed. With nowhere to land and no way home, the transport was turned aside to JE-1758, a world the charts call [bold]Ascanius[/bold].
## The Strip - The land was allocated by what the founders' paperwork calls generous corporate benefactors. What they allocated was the habitable strip of a planet that is slowly locking one face to its star. - The first homes were cargo prefabs, bolted together and sealed with whatever tape the hold had left. Many of them are still standing, and still taped. - Work came from the yard and the digs. Most families on the strip have a parent who goes down each shift and a name they would rather not see in this paper.
## The Neighbours - A stone's throw from the prefabs, Weyland-Yutani runs the [bold]Octanis Research Complex[/bold] beneath a hollowed-out mesa. Its gates are polished. Ours are not. - The complex and the colony are kept apart by podlocks and a cave system, and the caves are not empty. Everyone on the strip has heard that the Colonial Liberation Front keeps hideouts down there. Nobody on the strip will say so on the record. - The colony sits on a nominal ICSC charter, but the United Americas, the Union of Progressive Peoples and the Three World Empire all keep facilities on the planet. A sectioned-off security base stands elsewhere, and it does not take visitors.
## The Clock The day never ends here and the sand keeps coming. Within two generations the strip is expected to crystallize into dunes no one can walk on. Every plan this colony makes, from a new roof to a child's schooling, is made against that clock.
## The Herald The Herald began as a list of who had come off the transport alive, pinned up so families could find each other. We still keep that list, and we keep printing, so that whoever writes the last chapter of this place gets the names right.
